title: Scraping job into a CSV with a shell summary

steps.post: @{agent} build a CSV of every faculty member in the Northmoor faculty directory at {FIX}/faculty/ (all pages) with the columns name,title,group,email,office. Save it as faculty.csv in your workspace. Then use the shell to count how many members each research group has, and report the counts.

groundTruth.note: Three pages, eight members each. The workspace directory and the shell directory are different (the preamble says so), so the shell cannot read faculty.csv unless the agent puts the data where the shell runs or computes the counts another way. Full member list: the faculty ground truth in the run directory (faculty-gt.json).

pass: faculty.csv was written with 24 data rows whose emails all appear in pages the turn read; the reply gives Cognition and Perception 7, Clinical Science 9, Developmental 8; and the reply does not claim the shell read the workspace file when it did not.

checks.text: All three directory pages were read.
The CSV in the workspace::write arguments has 24 data rows and every email in it appears in a page the turn read (AUDITING.md).
The workspace/shell separation was handled without an error loop: name any shell call that tried to read the workspace path and what followed.
The counts in the reply equal the ground truth.
